texts.li: {A_nameDef} owned up to eating the chocolate {B_nameDef} had been saving, and {B_nameDef} took a long breath and let it go.
{A_nameDef} admitted to {B_nameDef} that {A_pronoun} had broken {B_nameDef}'s good mug a month ago and hidden the pieces.
{A_nameDef} confessed to knocking {B_nameDef}'s washing into the dirt and blaming it on the wind.
{B_nameDef} finally learned why {B_possessive} chair wobbles: {A_nameDef} had stood on it to reach a shelf.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} who had used up the last of the good soap, and {B_nameDef} said {B_pronoun} had guessed.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {A_possessive} real name, the one from before, and {B_nameDef} promised never to use it.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the lock of hair sewn into the lining of {A_possessive} coat, and told {B_objective} whose it was.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} why {A_pronoun} really left home, and it was not the story {A_nameDef} usually tells.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} a scar {A_pronoun} keeps covered, and told {B_objective} how it happened.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the child {A_pronoun} left behind, and asked {B_objective} never to mention it.
{B_nameDef} was dead on {B_possessive} feet, so {A_nameDef} took {B_possessive} night watch and sent {B_objective} off to rest.
{A_nameDef} took over {B_nameDef}'s hauling and told {B_objective} to sit down for a while.
Unasked, {A_nameDef} took on {B_nameDef}'s share of the work along with {A_possessive} own.
{A_nameDef} saw how tired {B_nameDef} looked and took the next job off {B_possessive} hands.
{B_nameDef} went to do {B_possessive} chores and found that {A_nameDef} had already done them.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} came to shouting over three smokeleaf joints owed since last winter.
{A_nameDef} found out that {B_nameDef} had repeated a confidence, and said so, loudly.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued until one of them said the thing that can't be taken back.
{A_nameDef} brought up one broken promise of {B_nameDef}'s, and it turned into every promise either of them had ever broken.
{B_nameDef} laughed at {A_nameDef} at the wrong moment, and {A_nameDef} hasn't let it go.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef}, too lightly, whether {B_pronoun} still had time for old friends.
{B_nameDef} has a new favorite person to eat with these days, and {A_nameDef} has started eating alone.
{B_nameDef} mentioned a new friend once too often, and {A_nameDef} has decided not to like this person.
{A_nameDef} made a sharp remark about {B_nameDef}'s new friend, then looked sorry {A_pronoun} had.
{B_nameDef} has been spending {B_possessive} evenings with someone new, and {A_nameDef} has started going to bed early.
{A_nameDef}'s favorite hammer snapped at the handle, and {A_nameDef} is sure {B_nameDef} had sawn it half through.
{A_nameDef} is certain {B_nameDef} has been moving {A_possessive} tools around on purpose.
{A_nameDef} blamed {B_nameDef} for a row of trampled seedlings, and {B_nameDef} swears it was only a shortcut.
{A_nameDef}'s blanket turned up in the dirt, and {A_nameDef} has blamed {B_nameDef} for it, loudly.
{A_nameDef} found dirt caked on {A_possessive} good knife and is sure {B_nameDef} has been digging with it.
{A_nameDef} bragged of killing a warg with a frying pan, and {B_nameDef} said {B_pronoun} had once killed two, with the lid.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} compared old injuries, each one worse than the last, until anyone nearby had moved away.
For every story {A_nameDef} told, {B_nameDef} had a bigger one ready, and neither would be the first to stop.
{A_nameDef} brought up the time {A_pronoun} crossed a desert on foot, and {B_nameDef} talked straight over {A_objective} about a worse one.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about which of them had nearly died more often.
{B_nameDef} looked over {A_nameDef}'s work, said nothing at all, and nodded once.
{B_nameDef} tasted {A_nameDef}'s cooking, paused, and asked if there was more.
Through clenched teeth, {B_nameDef} admitted that {A_nameDef} had done the job better than {B_pronoun} could have.
{B_nameDef} conceded that {A_nameDef} had been right, and changed the subject quickly.
{B_nameDef} borrowed a tool from {A_nameDef} and didn't complain about how it was kept, which counts as praise.
At dinner, {A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef}, loudly, whether {B_pronoun} had cooked the stew or just sat in it.
{A_nameDef} raised a cup at dinner "to {B_nameDef}, who has never once been the reason we won a fight."
{A_nameDef} told the whole table that {B_nameDef} snores like a dying muffalo, and {B_nameDef} left {B_possessive} meal half eaten.
{A_nameDef} pushed the smallest bowl across to {B_nameDef}, "since {B_pronoun} does the least work."
{A_nameDef} asked the table whether anyone else could smell {B_nameDef} from where they sat.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} ended up nose to nose, and for a long moment neither of them backed off.
{B_nameDef} knocked {A_nameDef}'s arm, maybe on purpose, and both of them squared up with their fists clenched.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} to say it again. {B_nameDef} said it again.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} grabbed for the same tool, and neither would let go.
{B_nameDef} laughed at {A_nameDef}'s mistake one time too many, and {A_nameDef} turned round slowly with {A_possessive} fists closed.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} sparred with sticks until both of them were limping and grinning.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the move that saved {A_possessive} life in the last fight, slowly at first and then at full speed.
A wrestling match between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} ended with both of them in the dirt and neither admitting defeat.
Counting every hit, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} practiced blocks with padded sticks.
{A_nameDef} woke shouting in the night, back in the last fight, and {B_nameDef} sat with {A_objective} until it was light.
{B_nameDef} found {A_nameDef} awake in the small hours, weapon in hand, and stayed with {A_objective} until sunrise.
{B_nameDef} heard {A_nameDef} giving orders in {A_possessive} sleep, back in the last fight, and woke {A_objective} gently.
{A_nameDef} stitched the reopened cut on {B_nameDef}'s arm, not very neatly, telling terrible jokes the whole time.
{A_nameDef} spotted the graze {B_nameDef} had been hiding since the fight, swore at {B_objective}, and cleaned it properly.
{A_nameDef} changed the dressing on {B_nameDef}'s leg and told {B_objective} off for walking on it.
{B_nameDef} kept getting one step of {SKILL} wrong until {A_nameDef} had to walk off and stare at a wall.
{A_nameDef} tried five different ways to explain {SKILL} to {B_nameDef}, and none of them took.
{A_nameDef} went over the same point of {SKILL} until {A_possessive} voice gave out, and {B_nameDef} still did it backward.
{B_nameDef} did work in {SKILL} better than {A_nameDef} could have, and {A_nameDef} said so out loud.
{A_nameDef} went over {B_nameDef}'s work in {SKILL} twice, looking for mistakes, and found none.
{B_nameDef} solved a problem in {SKILL} that {A_nameDef} had given up on long ago, and showed {A_objective} how.
{B_nameDef} asked a question about {SKILL} that {A_nameDef} couldn't answer, so they worked it out together.
{B_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} a trick in {SKILL} of {B_possessive} own, and {A_nameDef} frowned, then took it up too.
{B_nameDef} found a quicker way round a problem in {SKILL}, and {A_nameDef} asked {B_objective} to show it twice.
{B_nameDef}'s lesson in {SKILL} went so badly that {A_nameDef} called it off halfway through.
{B_nameDef} did exactly what {A_nameDef} had said not to do, and the lesson in {SKILL} turned into a cleanup.
{A_nameDef} confidently showed {B_nameDef} how it's done in {SKILL}, got it all wrong, and swore {B_objective} to secrecy.
{A_nameDef} lost the thread halfway through a lesson in {SKILL}, and {B_nameDef} had to remind {A_objective} where they were.
An argument about the right way to tame a boomalope kept {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talking long after it stopped being one.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} found they had both been naming the wild animals that wander past, and compared names.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} traded stories of the worst animal bites they had ever had.
{A_nameDef} complimented {B_nameDef}'s new haircut, but {B_nameDef} had not had a haircut, and took it as a dig.
{A_nameDef} waved at {B_nameDef}, and {B_nameDef} took it for a rude gesture.
{B_nameDef} thought {A_nameDef} was asking {B_objective} out, when {A_nameDef} had only wanted to borrow a knife.
{B_nameDef} tripped just as {A_nameDef} burst out laughing at something else, and took it personally.
{A_nameDef} called {B_nameDef}'s cooking "interesting" and meant it kindly, but {B_nameDef} didn't hear it that way.
{A_nameDef} borrowed {B_nameDef}'s good knife without asking and gave it back with a chip in the blade.
{A_nameDef} admitted to wearing {B_nameDef}'s coat while {B_pronoun} was busy, and said it had just been lying there.
The bedroll {A_nameDef} borrowed from {B_nameDef} for a hunt came back smelling of smoke and blood.
{B_nameDef}'s comb came back from {A_nameDef} with someone else's hair in it.
{A_nameDef} noticed {B_nameDef} looking grim and talked to {B_objective} about nothing in particular until {B_pronoun} smiled.
{A_nameDef} handed {B_nameDef} back {B_possessive} torn boots, mended.
{A_nameDef} brought {B_nameDef} a hot drink in the middle of a bad day, and left before {B_nameDef} could say thanks.
{A_nameDef} noticed {B_nameDef} hadn't eaten and pressed a piece of bread into {B_possessive} hand.
{A_nameDef} took {B_nameDef}'s turn at the worst job of the day and wouldn't hear a word about it.
{A_nameDef} studied {B_nameDef}'s haircut for a long moment and asked whether it had been done in the dark.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that {B_possessive} cooking was proof the colony could survive anything.
{A_nameDef} informed {B_nameDef}, at the top of {A_possessive} voice, that {B_pronoun} walks like a lame goat.
{A_nameDef} looked at {B_nameDef}'s patched coat and asked whether {B_pronoun} had lost a fight with a dog.
According to {A_nameDef}, {B_nameDef}'s singing is the reason the animals keep their distance.
{A_nameDef} remarked to {B_nameDef}, pleasantly, that people come apart much the same way muffalo do.
{B_nameDef} asked whether {A_nameDef} missed anyone from before, and {A_nameDef} gave it honest thought, said no, and smiled.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef}, in some detail, how long a body takes to stop smelling in this climate.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef}, with real interest, what {B_pronoun} would do if the food ran out and only one of them could eat.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have invented a secret language, mostly clicks and whistles, with a very rude word for grown-ups.
A box of treasures is buried somewhere, and only {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have the map.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have a secret signal for when a grown-up is coming, and use it constantly.
{A_nameDef} dared {B_nameDef} to hold {B_possessive} breath for a count of a hundred, and {B_nameDef} got to ninety.
On a dare from {A_nameDef}, {B_nameDef} said a rude word to a grown-up's face.
{A_nameDef} dared {B_nameDef} to eat a worm, and {B_nameDef} did, pulling faces the whole time.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} why the sky is that color and what the council is for, and got answers that were mostly true.
{A_nameDef} begged {B_nameDef} for a story until {B_nameDef} gave in with a long one about a giant squirrel.
{A_nameDef} insisted on helping {B_nameDef} with {B_possessive} work, and {B_nameDef} let {A_objective}, though it took three times as long.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} so many questions about the stars that {B_nameDef} promised to point them out to {A_objective} after dark.
{A_nameDef} has paced out the space where {B_nameDef} sleeps and found it a full step longer than {A_possessive} own.
{A_nameDef} praised {B_nameDef}'s bed through gritted teeth, then went and glared at {A_possessive} own.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} how {B_pronoun} had ended up with the better place to sleep, in a voice that wasn't really asking.
{A_nameDef} described an old fight to {B_nameDef} over dinner, wound by wound, until {B_nameDef} pushed {B_possessive} bowl away.
While {B_nameDef} was eating stew, {A_nameDef} explained what an axe does to a skull, sounds and all.
Between mouthfuls, {A_nameDef} explained to {B_nameDef} which wounds bleed most, in more detail than {B_nameDef} wanted.
{A_nameDef} explained {B_nameDef}'s own job to {B_objective}, slowly, and {B_nameDef} had to admit some of it was right.
{A_nameDef} corrected {B_nameDef}'s grammar halfway through a sentence, and {B_nameDef} forgot what {B_pronoun} had been saying.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how long {B_possessive} last job had taken, and how long it should have taken.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef}, a bit too eagerly, which of the colony's buildings would burn best.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about every fire {A_pronoun} had ever seen, eyes shining, and {B_nameDef} began edging toward the door.
{A_nameDef} explained to {B_nameDef} how to read a fire's heat from the color of its flame, and wouldn't let {B_objective} leave.
